subject: Mystic Avenue and Salem Street Zoning Proposals
overview: The committee reviewed proposed zoning updates for the Mystic Avenue and Salem Street corridors, focusing on increasing residential density and expanding public sidewalks through curb setbacks. Consultants presented tiered height recommendations and design standards intended to transform existing auto-oriented lots into walkable mixed-use developments.

items.title: Mystic Avenue Corridor Zoning Recommendations
items.summary: Innes Associates proposed a zoning framework for Mystic Avenue that utilizes 'curb setbacks' to create ten-foot sidewalks and green strips on private property in exchange for increased building heights. Proposed heights range from six stories near downtown to twelve stories on larger lots east of the corridor, with a focus on requiring active ground floors.

items.title: Planning Department Feedback and Draft Ordinance Requests
items.summary: Planning Director Alicia Hunt requested that the consultants provide rough draft language and bulleted design standards early to allow staff to evaluate the technical complexities of the proposed 'curb line' building requirements. The committee discussed the long-term vision of these changes, noting they would likely take decades to fully implement as parcels redevelop.

items.title: Salem Street Corridor Zoning Recommendations
items.summary: The committee reviewed a proposal for Salem Street that establishes density nodes at major intersections, such as the Target area, while maintaining residential-only zoning on specific blocks to preserve neighborhood character. Consultants recommended heights of up to six stories for mixed-use buildings, utilizing step-backs above the fourth floor to minimize the visual impact on the narrow streetscape.

items.title: Discussion on Salem Street Parcel Feasibility
items.summary: Planning staff expressed concern that Salem Street's smaller parcel sizes may make the proposed setbacks and high-density buildings difficult to build while maintaining project viability. Councilors debated the merits of four-story versus six-story limits, noting that height caps can significantly influence construction costs and the total number of housing units produced.

items.title: Project Timeline and Next Steps
items.summary: Chair Collins outlined the agenda for the September 11 meeting, which will cover the condo conversion ordinance, housing definitions, and incentive zoning strategies. A public participant spoke in favor of replacing 'asphalt desert' parking lots with multi-story mixed-use developments and supported setbacks to improve walkability.
